subject: design-technology
title: CAM and CNC
welcome_lead: Computer-aided manufacture — turning CAD into chips.
meta_desc: A-Level D&T: CAM, CNC and the digital factory.

concepts.def: Computer-Aided Manufacture — software generates machine code from CAD.
Computer Numerical Control — machines driven by G-code.
Standard programming language for CNC tool paths.
Sequence of co-ordinates the cutter follows.
Movement in X, Y, Z — standard CNC milling.
Adds two rotational axes (A, B) for complex surfaces.

walkthroughs.body_html: The CAD-CAM-CNC chain converts a 3D model to physical part. CAD designs the geometry; CAM generates the tool paths; the post-processor outputs G-code; the CNC machine executes.
Standard milling uses three linear axes (X, Y, Z). 5-axis machining adds two rotational axes (A, B), allowing single-setup machining of complex parts — used for turbine blades and medical implants.
CAM enables: repeatability (every part identical), 24/7 unmanned production, complex geometries impossible by hand, and direct iteration from CAD without re-drawing.

numericals.q: A 3-axis CNC has axes X, Y, Z. A 5-axis CNC has how many extra axes (beyond 3)?
